name: Abijam
bio:
Abijam (called Abijah throughout 2 Chronicles) was Rehoboam's son, who succeeded him as king of Judah after Rehoboam's seventeen-year reign ended and he was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 14:31). Of all his father's many children, Abijam was the one Rehoboam loved best, as the son of his favorite wife Maachah, daughter of Absalom; Rehoboam appointed him chief among his brothers and intended all along for him to be king (2 Chronicles 11:21-22). He reigned three years in Jerusalem; his mother was Maachah, daughter of Abishalom (called Michaiah, daughter of Uriel of Gibeah, in 2 Chronicles 13:2 — the same woman under a different name and lineage). Abijam committed all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not fully devoted to the LORD as David's had been — yet for David's sake the LORD preserved a lamp for him in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam throughout his reign (1 Kings 15:1-8).

Chronicles gives this war in full. Abijah marched out with 400,000 chosen men against Jeroboam's 800,000, and from Mount Zemaraim delivered a speech to Jeroboam and all Israel: the LORD had given the kingdom to David and his sons forever, and Jeroboam, once Solomon's own servant, had rebelled against his rightful lord with the backing of worthless men; Judah, by contrast, still kept the LORD's priesthood and worship, while Israel had cast out the sons of Aaron and the Levites for priests of their own making and golden calves. Jeroboam set an ambush that caught Judah's army front and back, but when Judah cried out to the LORD and the priests sounded their trumpets, the men of Judah shouted and God routed Jeroboam's army, killing 500,000 of Israel's chosen men. Abijah pressed his advantage, capturing Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron with their surrounding towns, and Jeroboam never recovered strength during Abijah's reign — Chronicles adds that the LORD himself struck Jeroboam down. Abijah grew powerful, marrying fourteen wives and fathering twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters, and his acts are recorded in the story of the prophet Iddo (2 Chronicles 13:1-22). When Abijam died, he was buried in the City of David, and his son Asa succeeded him (1 Kings 15:8).
